name: KRYQOVA Web Security
author: satrimtechnologies

sections.description:
KRYQOVA provides local security controls and visibility for single-site WordPress installations.

  • Brute-force protection with a failed-login limit of eight attempts per connection per 15 minutes.
  • Conservative firewall checks for suspicious URL patterns after WordPress loads.
  • Optional XML-RPC and application-password blocking.
  • Authenticator-based two-factor authentication (TOTP), encrypted secrets, replay protection and single-use recovery codes. Each user can enroll their own account under Users > Profile > KRYQOVA 2FA; administrators also have a dashboard section.
  • Administrator-only creation, editing, publishing, trash and deletion of protected editorial content through normal WordPress APIs.
  • Automatic resumable site-root scanning, official WordPress core checksum checks and suspicious code patterns.
  • Expanded execution, encoded JavaScript, hidden iframe, wrapped include and redirect heuristics; read-only inspection of native posts/excerpts, options, post meta, comments and user meta in bounded byte chunks.
  • Optional WPVulnerability component advisories with version-range matching, explicit unavailable/unknown coverage and cached official WordPress.org plugin checksums.
  • Atomic source/account login counters in addition to the existing connection transient limit. Additional request-body rules have learning/blocking modes; learning is the upgrade default.
  • Optional administrator 2FA policy with a seven-day enrollment grace period, local authenticator QR codes and current-account session revocation.
  • Administrator-confirmed upload quarantine, authenticated encrypted recovery copies and checksum-verified repair of individual official core files. No automatic deletion or repair.
  • Quick and full scans, configurable worker budget/pause/schedule, stalled-worker watchdog, finding severity/review workflow and JSON evidence export.
  • Retryable, concurrency-safe alert outbox; wp_mail acceptance/failure is recorded separately from delivery, which is not guaranteed.
  • Live scan counters, latest report, explicit protection readiness and completed-scan history in Overview.
  • View details window with local banner and Description, FAQ, Changelog and Screenshots tabs.

Editorial locking is opt-in on new installs; existing settings are retained. It targets posts, pages and WordPress/Elementor templates, while cron/CLI jobs and cleanup remain trusted. Products, orders, custom community/course types, comments and attachments are outside this restriction. Trusted administrator actions, direct database writes and compromised runtime code are outside its enforcement boundary.

No plugin prevents every attack or proves a site malware-free. Keep software updated and maintain off-site backups and a host/CDN firewall. This plugin does not provide comprehensive exploit signatures, IP reputation, edge/DDoS mitigation, automatic repair or inspection of every third-party database table. Its local heuristic rules require review and ongoing updates.

Automatic scans

A first scan is scheduled after activation, followed by full scans on the saved schedule (daily by default; hourly/twice-daily can be selected). Work is divided internally to respect hosting request limits, but it continues automatically; there is no manual batch button. While an administrator keeps the dashboard open, authenticated background requests advance the scan and refresh results. WP-Cron continues the scan with site traffic. For unattended operation on a low-traffic site or with DISABLE_WP_CRON, configure a server cron to invoke wp-cron.php.

All readable regular files under the WordPress root are streamed without a fixed file-count, directory-entry or file-size quota. The scan excludes symlinks, locations outside that root and live SQLite databases. Unreadable, removed or changing files, database errors and unavailable core checksums are reported as incomplete coverage. Core and component checksums stream file bytes for all readable sizes without loading entire files into PHP memory. A single hash operation can exceed the cooperative time budget on very large or slow files. A running site can change while it is scanned. Pattern matching cannot detect every unknown or obfuscated payload. The scanner never deletes or repairs files. Separate recovery actions require administrator permission, nonce, current password, an enrolled second factor and explicit confirmation.

Two-factor authentication

Open the 2FA section, enter your current password and begin setup. Scan the locally generated QR code or add the displayed manual setup key to a time-based authenticator account, then confirm a six-digit code. Save the ten recovery codes offline; they are shown once and each works once. Disabling 2FA or regenerating recovery codes requires both your current password and a valid authenticator/recovery code. Existing other sessions are revoked on enrollment. Application-password authentication is unavailable for enrolled accounts.

OpenSSL AES-256-GCM support is required for encrypted 2FA secrets. If unavailable, enrollment is disabled with an explanation. Secrets are encrypted using WordPress authentication salts; changing those salts requires recovery-code login and re-enrollment. Keep recovery codes before rotating salts.

Advanced firewall and login controls

Additional body rules default to learning mode, logging rule labels rather than blocking. Inspect your own login, forms, WooCommerce checkout and integrations before choosing Blocking in Advanced protection. Mode/policy changes require your current password and an enrolled second factor. Bodies are bounded to 128 KiB / 2,000 inspected values, exact password fields are excluded; token/nonce fields are inspected, administrator editor requests bypass additional rules, and multipart file contents use the existing upload checks. These are selected local heuristics, not a maintained global exploit-intelligence firewall.

Connection login throttling keeps its existing eight-attempt transient window and also uses atomic database counters: eight failed attempts per source per fixed 15-minute bucket and account counters are observations only and never deny authentication across connections. Boundaries reset the atomic counters; the existing rolling transient still applies. Proxy client IPs may be configured at the web server or through explicit trusted-proxy CIDRs and a selected forwarded header in Advanced protection. Headers from untrusted peers are ignored; X-Forwarded-For is walked right to left, never blindly trusting the first value. Optional login/REST request-rate observations flag above 120 requests per source per fixed minute. They block only in Blocking mode.

Upload admission

WordPress installer ZIPs require the exact upload workflow, capability, nonce and validated archive paths. Ordinary PHP, executable script and active document extensions are denied. Plain-text/CSV code examples are allowed. Other allowed files receive bounded head/tail inspection (up to 1 MiB each); large files are not rejected solely at 32 MiB. Sampling is not a full malware scan and cannot rule out content between the samples. WordPress MIME/type checks and hosting limits still apply.

Recovery and trusted baselines

Findings & recovery provides severity, location, recommended action and per-report acknowledged/false-positive review labels. These labels do not suppress detection or prove remediation. File changes are never automatic. Only an exact path from the latest findings is eligible; quarantine is limited to regular uploads files and rejects symlinks and traversal. A committed AES-256-GCM encrypted original is stored in a dedicated chunk table (legacy option copies remain readable) before removing or overwriting the active file. Core repair fetches an official released-version source file and verifies its official checksum before writing. Replacement failures retain the original recovery copy. Restore verifies ciphertext/authentication and refuses to overwrite unrelated newer files.

Portable recovery export requires a separate 16–256 character passphrase and re-encrypts originals with PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256 (210,000 rounds) and AES-256-GCM. Keep the export and passphrase off-site. The included offline-recovery-reader.py.txt requires Python 3 with cryptography; it extracts numbered .bin files for offline review and never executes or restores them. Old copies without authenticated metadata retain legacy compatibility; new copies authenticate the path and recovery metadata.

Limits: 10 MiB per recovery file, 20 saved files and 50 MiB original bytes total. Copies are not exposed as public web files. WordPress authentication salt rotation invalidates them; maintain independent backups first. Plugin Delete preserves data by default; explicit permanent removal deletes recovery copies; restore or independently back up required files before uninstalling. Restoring a quarantined file can restore malicious code. Only do it after reviewing the original. Premium/custom plugin/theme repair and database cleanup are manual developer/host tasks.

A manually established local baseline trusts plugin/theme hashes from a completed full scan, after the administrator confirms those files are clean. Future changed, added and missing files are findings. A partial scan cannot establish a new trusted baseline. This is change detection, not certification of the baseline. Cached official plugin checksums provide vendor comparison where available. Themes/custom components without official checksums remain explicitly unverified.

Privacy and retention

Audit logs contain event time, user ID, short sanitized details and a keyed hash of the connection IP. Retention is 30 days with daily cleanup. Scan reports contain paths and finding categories; the most recent 14 scan summaries and indexed evidence sets are retained, plus the trusted baseline and active scan. Reports embed at most 500 findings; Findings & recovery searches all retained findings for the latest scan. Activity searches and JSON exports include all retained events. Job state stores paths and offsets, never source file contents. Authenticator secrets are encrypted; recovery codes are password-hashed. Deactivation keeps settings and evidence; With explicit permanent-removal opt-in, WordPress Delete removes this plugin’s settings, tables, authenticator records and temporary data and encrypted recovery copies. It does not perform additional filesystem changes during uninstall; previously quarantined files remain absent until explicitly restored.

Live-audit corrections

Scans retain their trigger and initiating user across background workers. Failed-login observations are limited to one per connection per minute, with separate lockout events; other security layers may reject requests before WordPress emits the login hook. Readiness warns about common overlapping security plugins and explains component-integrity/2FA/cron setup. Optional public-user privacy restricts logged-out users REST endpoints and numeric author-ID lookups; it is off by default. Upload PHP location alone is a review signal, while suspicious execution content is evaluated separately. See OPERATOR-GUIDE.txt.

Review controls and privacy

Firewall exceptions expire after seven days, match one body rule, exact field, POST path, AJAX action and REST route (where applicable), and do not disable upload checks, rate limits or URL protection. Administrator login-source history stores up to ten keyed hashes per account. A new connection is a review signal, not proof of compromise. Test email uses the configured administrator email and is limited to once per five minutes.

Source code

Human-readable JavaScript and CSS source is included in assets/. The shipped files are used directly; no compilation, bundling or minification step is required. Edit these files directly to modify the plugin. The local QR generator in assets/vendor/qrcode.js retains its author, license and source information; see assets/vendor/LICENSE.txt.

External services

Core integrity and repair networking is disabled by default on new installs and upgrades. An administrator must explicitly enable “Allow external core verification and repair downloads” in Advanced protection and save the nonce-protected settings form. Disabling it stops future core requests. Local scans continue with incomplete core verification reported. After opt-in, core integrity scans retrieve official checksum data from https://api.wordpress.org/core/checksums/1.0/ using the WordPress safe HTTP API. The request includes WordPress version and locale. No files, audit logs, passwords, recovery codes or 2FA secrets are uploaded. See https://wordpress.org/about/privacy/ for WordPress.org privacy information. Optional component intelligence is disabled until the administrator consents. It requests https://www.wpvulnerability.net/core/{version}/, /plugin/{slug}/ and /theme/{slug}/. The WordPress version and installed component slugs, plus the server connection IP and normal HTTP metadata, are disclosed. No source files, database content, logs or credentials are uploaded. Privacy: https://www.wpvulnerability.com/privacy/ ; service documentation/terms: https://www.wpvulnerability.com/ and https://docs.wpvulnerability.com/ . Responses are cached up to six hours; failed/unknown/range-unsupported responses are coverage notices. A historical report is not proof the current component version remains safe.

With the same consent, official plugin hashes are fetched from https://downloads.wordpress.org/plugin-checksums/{slug}/{version}.json and cached up to a day. This discloses plugin slug/version to WordPress.org. Core-file repair service (core.svn.wordpress.org): core recovery explicitly requested by an administrator downloads from https://core.svn.wordpress.org/tags/{installed-version}/{relative-file} and verifies official core checksums before writing. The repair request discloses the installed WordPress version, relative core-file path, server connection IP and standard HTTP metadata to WordPress.org; it does not upload the local file. This request requires the separate core verification/repair opt-in as well as administrator confirmation of the repair. Component-intelligence consent does not enable core requests. WordPress.org privacy: https://wordpress.org/about/privacy/ ; service information: https://wordpress.org/about/ . Source and hashes are trusted over HTTPS; custom/localized builds may not have a matching replacement and are refused.

Dashboard scripts, QR generation, charts, banners and screenshots are bundled locally; no remote scripts are loaded into the interface. No telemetry is sent. Core-file repair retrieves official replacement files only for an explicitly confirmed repair.
sections.installation:
1. Back up and test on staging. Requires single-site WordPress 6.7+ and PHP 7.4+.
  2. Upload kryqova-web-security-2.2.9.zip using Plugins > Add New > Upload Plugin, then activate. Do not upload the separate directory-assets ZIP.
  3. Open KRYQOVA. The scan proceeds automatically; no batch processing action is required.
  4. Review protection settings and enroll your own authenticator under Two-factor authentication.
  5. From the Plugins screen, use View details for the banner and information tabs, or Screenshots for the included gallery.

This directory package uses kryqova-web-security. If upgrading a legacy cybersentrix installation, back up first and deactivate it before activating this package. Do not delete the inactive legacy copy through WordPress: its uninstall routine shares storage and can erase the new copy’s saved data. Settings and logs are retained on normal upgrades. Earlier branded packages are imported into separate storage and disabled during activation. Verify imported records before deleting inactive older packages. An earlier in-progress scan is restarted with the new engine.
sections.faq:
Must I process the next scan batch?

No. Scan work continues through WP-Cron and the authenticated dashboard worker. A complete readable site-root scan can span many automatic requests on a large site. Skipped paths and incomplete verification remain visible.

Does Overview update after a scan?

Yes. The dashboard worker updates counters and reloads the completed report and scan history when a scan finishes. Background scans are also shown when the dashboard is next loaded. If you have unsaved settings, save them before refreshing.

What does the firewall protect?

It checks conservative URL patterns such as traversal, executable wrappers, null bytes and sensitive-file probes after WordPress loads. Login limits reduce repeated password attempts. Use a host/CDN firewall for edge filtering and broader threat intelligence.

Does it support multisite?

No. The current package supports single-site WordPress.

Is 2FA mandatory for every account?

No. It is enabled per account after the owner verifies an authenticator. Users can access their own 2FA enrollment page from their profile. Administrators should enroll every privileged account separately.

How can I recover access?

Use an unused recovery code or wait for a login lockout to expire. If needed, a hosting administrator can rename wp-content/plugins/kryqova-web-security to disable the plugin. There is no public unauthenticated bypass URL.

Does uploading the ZIP create a WordPress.org listing?

No. Directory publication needs a real WordPress.org account, submission, manual review and an assigned repository. The local View details window and included screenshots work without a public listing.
sections.changelog:
2.2.9

  • Align the storage helper class with the existing plugin class prefix; retain all storage keys and migration behaviour.

2.2.8

  • Add separate explicit opt-in for core checksum requests and repair downloads. Local scans remain available without external services.
  • Bundle readable asset source and document the no-build workflow.
  • Remove directory banners from the installable package and remove an unused core include.
  • Retain administrator permission and nonce checks for settings and privileged actions.

2.2.7

  • Rename all 14 short transient families to kryqova_ with expiry-preserving legacy reads and safe dual-name deletion.
  • Document external services, including administrator-requested core.svn.wordpress.org repair downloads.
  • Verify PHP 7.4, 8.0 and 8.1 compatibility.

2.2.6

  • Narrow request-call detection to adjacent same-line code and exclude comments and string examples.
  • Suppress heuristic file alerts only after a stable official checksum match; changed and unverified files remain scanned.

2.2.5

  • Add explicitly configured trusted proxy CIDRs and strict forwarded-address handling.
  • Store new encrypted originals in a dedicated 32 KiB chunk table; retain legacy reads.
  • Keep plugin data on uninstall unless permanent deletion is explicitly enabled.
  • Batch short database rows and reduce idle/hidden dashboard polling.

2.2.4

  • Make editorial locking opt-in for new installs; preserve cron/CLI housekeeping and custom community content.
  • Replace broad primitive capability removal with per-object editorial checks.
  • Remove account-wide hard login lockouts; retain connection throttling.
  • Narrow SQL grammar, inspect token-named fields, and expand request-controlled execution heuristics.
  • Exclude internal audit documentation from the distributed archive.

2.2.3

  • Verify large core/component files with bounded-memory hash streams.
  • Retain scan trigger and initiator across background workers.
  • Record failed-login events with bounded repetition and warn about overlapping login controls.
  • Correct recovery instructions and classify uploads by content evidence and location separately.
  • Add setup guidance for component integrity, 2FA and server cron.

2.2.2

  • Match the directory submission slug, main file and translation domain.
  • Correct Tested up to metadata to major/minor format 7.1.

2.2.1

  • Validate scalar request input before sanitizing or password verification.
  • Review security, escaping, sanitization, nonce and directory guideline boundaries.

2.2.0

  • Remediate the internal audit compatibility, scan, recovery, history and UI findings.
  • Add WooCommerce 2FA inputs and exact action/route/field firewall exceptions.
  • Replace fixed-size upload rejection with type-aware bounded admission inspection.
  • Store component inventory and complete findings in an indexed table.
  • Add retained-history search, full streamed exports, atomic file replacement and portable encrypted recovery copies.
  • Preserve configured scan frequency; remove duplicate role events.

2.1.0

  • Add expiring exact-path POST firewall rule exceptions with identity confirmation.
  • Add administrator connection alerts, session summaries and a rate-limited mail test.
  • Explain finding evidence and display active scan stages and worker freshness.
  • Expand encoded injection detection and regression samples.

  • Retain software upload correction and existing integrity verification.

  • Fix legitimate administrator theme/plugin ZIP uploads with nonce, capability and archive validation.

  • Keep ordinary media upload script protection enabled.

  • Remove duplicate banner title; retain the native WordPress heading.

  • Renamed to KRYQOVA Web Security with refreshed branding and screenshots.

  • Preserved existing plugin settings, logs and 2FA enrollment.

  • Expanded code heuristics and bounded native database-content scanning.

  • Consented vulnerability inventory and official plugin checksums; optional component baseline.
  • Learning/blocking body rules, atomic login counters and optional endpoint rate observations.
  • Administrator 2FA policy/grace period, local QR enrollment and session revocation.
  • Encrypted upload quarantine, checksum-verified core repair and guarded restore.
  • Configurable quick/full scan scheduling/resources and stalled-worker watchdog.
  • Actionable finding review, protection readiness, JSON export and retryable alert digest.
  • Additional WordPress/PHP/MariaDB, security and browser regression checks. External independent audit remains pending.

  • Link the author attribution to https://www.satrimtechnologies.co.za in the Plugins screen and View details.

  • Author changed to Satrim Technologies.
  • Faster full scans: bulk file discovery, prefetched queue jobs, time-budgeted workers and shorter automatic continuation delays.

Core-file repair service (core.svn.wordpress.org): core recovery explicitly requested by an administrator downloads from https://core.svn.wordpress.org/tags/{installed-version}/{relative-file} and verifies official core checksums before writing. The repair request discloses the installed WordPress version, relative core-file path, server connection IP and standard HTTP metadata to WordPress.org; it does not upload the local file. This request requires the separate core verification/repair opt-in as well as administrator confirmation of the repair. Component-intelligence consent does not enable core requests. WordPress.org privacy: https://wordpress.org/about/privacy/ ; service information: https://wordpress.org/about/ . Source and hashes are trusted over HTTPS; custom/localized builds may not have a matching replacement and are refused.

Dashboard scripts, QR generation, charts, banners and screenshots are bundled locally; no remote scripts are loaded into the interface. No telemetry is sent. Core-file repair retrieves official replacement files only for an explicitly confirmed repair.
